description.summary: screencasts served by the window manager

protocol.description:
This fork-only protocol (newm-river, a fork of river) hands the window manager the screencast requests river receives on the zkde_screencast_unstable_v1 global (KDE's protocol, which Spectacle records through with KPipeWire). The window manager captures the source (with ext-image-copy-capture-v1, say), produces a PipeWire stream and answers with its node id, which river forwards to the client.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: newm_river_screencast_v1
interface.description: Only the client that is the active window manager receives requests: river relays to the newest newm_river_screencast_v1 bound by the client that owns the river_window_manager_v1 object. While there is none, river fails every zkde_screencast_unstable_v1 stream at once.

request.name: destroy
request.description: No more requests are relayed to this object. Casts already created are not affected.

event.name: stream_output

description.summary: a client asks for a stream of an output

event.description: The source is the output called output_name (wl_output.name). pointer is the zkde_screencast_unstable_v1.pointer value the client asked for.

event.name: stream_window

description.summary: a client asks for a stream of a window

event.description: window_uuid is the string the client passed, unchanged: the window manager gave it out (as org.kde.KWin's window uuid, say) and resolves it.

event.name: stream_region

description.summary: a client asks for a stream of a region

event.description: A rectangle in the global logical coordinate space. scale 0 lets the window manager choose.

interface.name: newm_river_screencast_cast_v1
interface.description: The window manager answers once with created or failed, and may later send closed when the source goes away. River forwards each to the client's zkde_screencast_stream_unstable_v1. Destroying a cast that was never answered fails the client's stream; destroying an answered one closes it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The window manager no longer serves this stream.

request.name: created
request.description: node is the PipeWire node id of the stream.

request.name: failed
request.description: A human readable reason, forwarded to the client.

request.name: closed
request.description: The source went away or the window manager stopped the stream.

event.name: stopped
event.description: The client destroyed its zkde_screencast_stream_unstable_v1. The window manager should stop the PipeWire stream and destroy the cast.
